sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in West Milford?
sections.html:
West Milford is a very large, lake-dotted township in northern Passaic County, and the sale hinges on a fire-safety certificate from the township, an appeal calendar run by the Passaic County Board of Taxation, and a deed recorded in Paterson. Most houses here are owner-occupied, so your likely buyer is a family planning to live in the house, though investors do shop the area.

The sections below cover the township's size and housing numbers, what its land and lakes mean for a listing, the certificate every seller needs, and the tax and recording steps that follow a signed contract.

sections.h2: How big is West Milford and what do the housing figures show?
sections.html:
West Milford covers 75.93 square miles of land, which makes it the largest municipality in Passaic County and more than 40 percent of the county's area. About 25,216 people lived there in mid-2025 according to the Census Bureau estimate, spread at roughly 327 people per square mile. Drivers often need close to 40 minutes to get to work.

Nearly 95 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so turnover is low and buyers compare your house with a small pool of recent sales. Ask a local agent for sold prices near your lake or road rather than leaning on the township median.

sections.h2: How did West Milford's history and land shape its homes?
sections.html:
The township was carved out of Pompton Township in 1834 and takes its name from a post office mix-up: a clerk reportedly gave the name West Milford to the western of two places called New Milford. Before World War II it was a resort area with rail stations at Charlotteburg, Newfoundland, Oak Ridge, Hewitt and Awosting, and steamboats on Greenwood Lake. After the war the summer cottages around the lakes slowly turned into year-round homes.

That history explains the housing you see today. Many houses sit on or near small lakes such as Upper Greenwood Lake, Wonder Lake and Lake Lockover, and the four main communities are the township center, Hewitt, Newfoundland and Oak Ridge. Greenwood Lake itself is about nine miles long and crosses into New York.

  • Large tracts around the Pequannock watershed belong to the City of Newark, so they will never be built on.
  • The 2004 Highlands Water Protection and Planning Act places the township in the Highlands preservation area, which adds state rules. Ask the township's land use staff before you promise a buyer an addition or a new lot.
  • Jungle Habitat, a safari park that ran from 1972 to 1976, became state land in 1988 and is now a mountain biking area, which is a selling point for outdoor buyers.

sections.h2: Which roads, buses and schools matter to West Milford buyers?
sections.html:
Route 23 is the main highway through the township, with County Routes 511 and 513 as the other major roads. The township counted 198.30 miles of roadway in 2010, of which 163.20 miles were township roads and most of the rest are county or state roads, so ask which agency maintains the road in front of your house. NJ Transit buses 194 and 196 run to the Port Authority Bus Terminal in Manhattan, and the township runs two limited local routes of its own.

West Milford Township Public Schools serve prekindergarten through grade 12 with elementary schools, Macopin Middle School and West Milford High School. Enrollment was 3,028 in the 2021-22 school year, and Westbrook Elementary closed ahead of the 2023-24 year. Students may also apply to Passaic County Technical Institute. Parents on a listing tour will ask which elementary school serves a given street, so confirm that with the district before you advertise it.

sections.h2: What certificate does West Milford require before a house is sold?
sections.html:
West Milford requires a Certificate of Smoke Alarm and Carbon Monoxide Alarm Compliance from the Fire Prevention Bureau before a one- or two-family home is sold, and selling without it can bring a fine of up to $2,500 under the state Uniform Fire Code. The state rule is N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.3. Book the inspection early, because certifications are scheduled on Wednesdays.

  • Fees under the township's February 2025 sheet: $55 when requested more than 10 business days before closing, $100 for four to ten business days, and $165 for under four business days. A re-inspection costs $50 more.
  • Alarms must be listed by UL and less than 10 years old, and sealed 10-year batteries are required on battery-only units.
  • A CO alarm is required in any home with a fuel-burning appliance, fireplace, wood stove or attached garage.
  • House numbers at least four inches tall must be visible from the street, or no certificate is issued.
  • Homes with solar panels, generators or battery backups need a label near the electric panel and meter reading "CAUTION: MULTIPLE SOURCES OF POWER."
  • The fire extinguisher requirement for one- and two-family homes ended February 3, 2025. The certificate is valid for six months and cannot be transferred.

The bureau is at 13 Edgar Drive and takes calls at 973-728-2840.

sections.h2: How do property tax assessments and appeals work in West Milford?
sections.html:
The township assessor mails assessment postcards each February 1, and a regular appeal must reach the Passaic County Board of Taxation by April 1 of the tax year. The county's 2026 regular deadline was April 1, 2026.

Appeals of added or omitted assessments, which arise when new construction or a change is added to the roll mid-year, are due by December 1 of the tax year. Forms are available from the West Milford assessor at 973-728-2793, and the county Board of Taxation sits at 930 Riverview Drive, Suite 250, in Totowa.

If you sell during the year, the closing statement will split the tax bill between you and the buyer. Ask the township tax collector for the current quarter's status and any sewer or lien balance before the closing date so the title company has an exact payoff.

sections.h2: Where is a West Milford deed recorded and what does the seller pay?
sections.html:
Deeds for West Milford go to the Passaic County Clerk's Registry Division at 401 Grand Street, Room 113, in Paterson. The office requires the words "Prepared by" on the deed, the tax block, lot and consideration, and a return address. An official county cover sheet is required or a $20 charge applies, and the county adds a $5 homelessness trust fund charge per document.

The state charges the seller a realty transfer fee when the deed is recorded. For a sale over $350,000, the first $150,000 is charged at $2.90 per $500, the next $50,000 at $4.25 per $500 and the band from $200,000 to $550,000 at $4.80 per $500, with higher bands above that. Your closing attorney or title agent will calculate the exact figure and pay it with a trust account check.

sections.h2: What are my choices for selling a West Milford house?
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell it yourself, or accept an as-is cash offer, and each route still needs the smoke and CO certificate, a clear title and a recorded deed.

  • Listing with an agent usually earns the widest buyer pool, which helps on lake and woodland lots that appeal to people from the New York area. It also means showings, inspections and a financing contingency that can stretch the timeline.
  • Selling on your own saves a commission but puts pricing, disclosures and contract review on you.
  • A cash buyer can close faster and skip repairs, which suits an inherited house, a property with deferred maintenance or an owner who has already moved.

Compare written offers by the amount you keep after the certificate fee, taxes, the transfer fee and any repairs you would otherwise pay for.

faqs.q: Do I need a certificate to sell my house in West Milford?
faqs.a: Yes for a one- or two-family home. The township's Fire Marshal issues a smoke and carbon monoxide alarm compliance certificate, and the township sheet lists fees of $55, $100 or $165 depending on how close to closing you apply. It lasts six months and cannot be passed to the buyer.

faqs.q: Can I sell a West Milford house that needs major repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. The certificate covers alarms, house numbers and a few other items rather than the condition of the whole house, so repairs do not have to be finished first. Buyers' lenders may insist on repairs, while a cash buyer can take the house as it stands.

faqs.q: When is the deadline to appeal a West Milford property tax assessment?
faqs.a: The regular deadline is April 1 of the tax year, filed with the Passaic County Board of Taxation after the February postcard arrives. Added or omitted assessment appeals are due December 1. The township assessor at 973-728-2793 can hand you the forms.

faqs.q: Where do I record the deed after a West Milford sale?
faqs.a: The Passaic County Clerk's Registry Division in Paterson records it, at 401 Grand Street, Room 113. Your closing attorney or title company normally handles this, along with the seller's realty transfer fee.

faqs.q: Does the Highlands Act affect selling a West Milford home?
faqs.a: It can. West Milford lies in the Highlands preservation area, so additions and new lots face additional state rules. An existing house sells like any other, but ask the township before you tell a buyer a teardown or expansion is possible.
